claims.text: The three primary artifacts describe one and the same trip, not three different ones: EV-TRIP-00113, EV-GPS-00113 and EV-FARE-00113 each carry trip_id TRP-00113, and the trace's first fix at 18:47:10 matches the trip_record's started_at, so the rider's limb-(a) identification burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged on the face of the record.

Nothing in the trace needs discounting in the rider's favour or against it: coverage is 100%, there are 217 fixes at the nominal 10-second sampling interval, the gaps array is empty and max_gap_sec is 0.0, so none of POL-RD-07(a), (b) or (c) fires, the trace is unimpaired for policy purposes, and the driven distance can be read straight off the trace without any gap-handling concession.

Under POL-RD-01 the governing distance field is gps_trace.trace_distance_km, not the rounded trip_record convenience copy, and the trace records 20.18 km against the optimal route of 19.40 km stored on the trip_record: the measured excess is 0.78 km, or 4.02%.

POL-RD-12 excuses only distance attributable to collecting or setting down a co-rider, and in this case that distance is already inside the 19.40 km matched-itinerary baseline the rider was notified of at 18:42:04; the clause's own closing words are that it 'does not excuse excess beyond the matched itinerary', and the trace still runs 0.78 km beyond that matched baseline.

The diversion is the driver's own route and is corroborated independently of the rider's account: the driver wrote in the chat log at 19:03:15 'pool booking, picking up the other passenger, app route', and the rider's sole message in the log is the query 'why are we at hougang' at 19:02:40 — the rider contributed no route instruction at all.

No traffic advisory carries the diversion: EV-ADVIS-00113-01 is MISSING, holds weight 0.0, and its issue code is MISSING_ARTIFACT, with no LTA advisory covering the Punggol, Hougang or CTE corridors in the 18:41-19:23 window on 5 August 2026, so POL-RD-03's closure exoneration is unavailable to the driver.

The detour cannot be shifted onto the rider: the chat log contains no rider instruction to divert and no message carries a waypoint_hint, so POL-RD-04 cannot be run in the driver's favour, its corroboration test is undecidable on this record, and the driver holds no rider-instruction exoneration.

This is not an upfront-quoted trip, so the route-deviation money has not been closed off: fare_breakdown.fare_model is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, POL-RD-11 does not apply, and POL-RD-02 is the operative remedy clause, which would run against the 19.40 km matched-itinerary figure and not the 15.80 km solo reference figure.

If the excess is made out, the POL-RD-02 quantum is not de minimis on the platform's own numbers: the fare_breakdown's recomputed_fare on the matched 19.40 km and 34 min is SGD 25.67, the difference from the SGD 26.83 charged is 1.16, and the amount payable rounds up to SGD 1.20, which is above the SGD 0.50 floor.

Neither profile can decide this case in either direction: the driver's deviation_flags_90d is 0 across 471 completed_trips_90d, so no POL-RD-06 repeat-deviation pattern is established on the only fields that clause names, and under POL-GEN-01 the driver's otherwise clean record is credibility weighting only and may not be used to establish any fact about this trip or to carry an adverse finding against the rider.

I do not stretch the arithmetic: measured on the governing trace the excess is 0.78 km, which does not exceed POL-RD-01's 0.8 km absolute gate, and 4.02%, which does not exceed its 20% gate, so on this trip's own evidence the route deviation as pleaded is not established and the POL-RD-01 finding properly reads 'no deviation'.

claims.text: This is a RYDE_POOL trip, so the only correct baseline for any deviation test is the matched-itinerary optimal that the platform computed and quoted at match time, 19.40 km on EV-TRIP-00113. The rider's arithmetic uses the 15.80 km solo_optimal_distance_km figure, which POL-RD-12 carries on the trip_record expressly 'for reference only' and which may not be used as the denominator of the POL-RD-01 test. A claim that measures excess against solo_optimal_distance_km has cited the wrong field and fails on that ground alone. Both figures are on the face of the record (optimal_distance_km 19.40; solo_optimal_distance_km 15.80), so the rider can see exactly why the 28% figure in the claim text is an artefact of the wrong comparator.

Measured the way POL-RD-01 requires, against the trace figure that governs and not the rounded convenience copy on the trip_record, the excess is 0.78 km. gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 20.18 km (EV-GPS-00113) and the matched-itinerary optimal is 19.40 km (EV-TRIP-00113), giving an excess of 0.78 km, or 4.02% of optimal. POL-RD-01 requires BOTH that the excess exceed 20% of optimal AND that it exceed 0.8 km absolute. This excess fails on both limbs: 4.02% is far below 20%, and 0.78 km is below the 0.8 km floor. No deviation is established, and no MATERIAL deviation is anywhere near established. POL-RD-01 then directs the outcome: NO_ACTION, however the rider characterises the trip.

Even on the rider's own theory that the Hougang leg is the objectionable part, POL-RD-12 excludes it before the threshold is applied: distance attributable to collecting a co-rider on a platform-matched pooled itinerary 'is never a deviation'. The record confirms the Hougang stop was precisely that — the driver's track is an unbroken 10-second telemetry trace (point_count 217, coverage_pct 100, gaps empty, max_gap_sec 0) whose only dwell is the co-rider boarding stop, and the driver's first and last fixes run 18:47:10 to 19:23:10 with no excursus off the matched corridor. The driver is not exonerated for going somewhere he chose; the stop he made was the itinerary the platform sold.

The route was disclosed to the rider in advance, in writing, by the platform itself. Chat message MSG-00113-001, sent 2026-08-05T18:42:04, states: 'Co-rider matched. Your pooled route now includes one pickup at Hougang Central before your drop-off. Estimated 19.4 km, 34 min.' It was read by the rider 27 seconds later, at 18:42:31, and the trip only started at 18:47:10. The claim that the driver 'went off to Hougang in the middle of my trip for no reason' is contradicted by the platform's own pre-trip notice; the Hougang pickup was announced before the vehicle moved. This is not a rider-instruction exoneration under POL-RD-04 — no waypoint_hint is present — but it is the factual answer to the only allegation of arbitrary conduct in the claim.

The rider's own chat entries corroborate the driver and defeat the claim's premise. At 19:02:40 the rider asks 'why are we at hougang'; the driver answers at 19:03:15 'pool booking, picking up the other passenger, app route'. That answer is consistent with the platform's 18:42:04 match notice, and it is the only party account of the Hougang stop anywhere on the record. The counterparty_statement is to the same effect. There is no artifact in the bundle that contradicts it, and no traffic advisory exists that could have forced the route (EV-ADVIS-00113-01 is MISSING; none covers the corridor). The driver's conduct was, on this record, exactly what POL-RD-12 describes and excuses.

The trace itself is unimpaired under POL-RD-07: coverage is 100%, the expected and actual sampling intervals both equal 10 seconds, there are no gaps recorded, and the maximum gap is 0.0 seconds. None of limbs (a), (b) or (c) fires, so the excess is measured from a clean trace and needs no independent corroboration. The GPS_TRACE artifact is also COMPLETE at weight 1.0, so there is no POL-GEN-02 discount to disclose or apply. The rider cannot argue the measurement is unsafe: it is the best-quality evidence in the bundle, and it is the artifact that defeats the claim.

The POL-RD-06 driver_profile check is not even reached, and where reached it is clean. The clause is consulted only where POL-RD-01 records a MATERIAL deviation or the evidence is otherwise finely balanced; here there is no deviation at all, let alone a material one, and the evidence is not balanced — one trace, one tolerance, both limbs failed. For completeness, the driver's trailing-90-day figure is deviation_flags_90d = 0 against completed_trips_90d = 471, so no pattern can be established on the fields the clause names, and POL-GEN-01 forbids substituting any other profile field for the test. No POL-RD-06(a) uplift, no POL-RD-06(b) FULL_REFUND uplift and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral is available to the rider on this record.

There is no alternative monetary route left to the rider. POL-RD-02 is the only clause that converts an established deviation into a refund, and no deviation is established, so the recomputation never runs. The fare-breakdown arithmetic confirms there is nothing else to correct: erp_lines carries no entries at all (total 0.00), the airport surcharge is 0.00 on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport, the promo_discount of 3.00 has already been subtracted from the charge, and the residual money comparison on EV-FARE-00113 yields a refund before rounding of only 1.16 against a charged_total of 26.83 — which is unreachable in any event because the threshold gate in POL-RD-01 fails. POL-GEN-03 then fixes the meaning of the outcome: the rider filed, the charge stands, the present state is preserved, and the ruling value is NO_ACTION.

The Hougang stop does not change this. It was the co-rider pickup on the pooled itinerary, announced to the rider by the platform at 18:42:04, before the vehicle moved, and POL-RD-12 excludes co-rider collection distance from excess in any event. ruling.explanation:
To the Rider and the Driver: this was a RYDE_POOL trip from Punggol to One Raffles Place on 5 August 2026, charged at SGD 26.83. The dispute is about how far the route strayed from the one the platform quoted.

Which baseline applies. Because this was a pooled booking, POL-RD-12 fixes the baseline as the matched-itinerary distance the platform computed and quoted when it matched the co-rider — 19.40 km (trip_record.optimal_distance_km). The 15.80 km the rider has used is the solo, unmatched estimate (solo_optimal_distance_km), which the same clause carries 'for reference only'. Measuring a pooled trip against the solo figure is the one thing POL-RD-12 says fails on its own ground, so the '28% longer' figure in the claim comes from the wrong comparator and cannot support a refund. The correct figures, 19.40 km matched against 15.80 km solo, are both on EV-TRIP-00113.

The threshold test. POL-RD-01 requires the governing distance to be read from the GPS trace, not the rounded trip-record copy. The trace records 20.18 km of travel (EV-GPS-00113) over the 19.40 km matched itinerary — an excess of 0.78 km, or 4.02%. A deviation is established only if the excess exceeds BOTH 20% of optimal AND 0.8 km in absolute terms. It fails both: 4.02% is far below 20%, and 0.78 km is below the 0.8 km gate. No deviation is established, and no MATERIAL deviation is in prospect.

The Hougang stop. The platform's own notice at 18:42:04, read by the rider at 18:42:31 and sent well before the vehicle moved at 18:47:10, stated: 'Co-rider matched. Your pooled route now includes one pickup at Hougang Central before your drop-off. Estimated 19.4 km, 34 min.' The stop was the matched co-rider pickup inside the itinerary the rider was sold; POL-RD-12 excludes co-rider collection distance before the threshold is applied. The driver's chat reply at 19:03:15 ('pool booking, picking up the other passenger, app route') and the driver's statement say the same thing. The rider's submission that this was the driver's own unannounced diversion is therefore not accepted — the platform disclosed it in writing before the trip began.

The trace. POL-RD-07: the trace is clean for policy purposes — 217 fixes at the nominal 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps, maximum gap 0.0 s. None of limbs (a)–(c) fires, so no gap concession or independent-corroboration requirement arises and the distance stands on its own. On the rider's point about the missing LTA advisory: its absence is noted, and it is the only artifact below full weight (EV-ADVIS-00113-01, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT). A MISSING artifact carries no fact. No party asserted a road closure, so no exculpatory clause was invoked and there is nothing for the missing advisory to exonerate — POL-RD-03 is not the operative clause here and POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged.

Money. Because no deviation is established, POL-RD-02's recomputation never runs: the 19.40 km recomputed fare of SGD 25.67 and the 1.16 difference the advocates quote are moot, and the de minimis question does not arise. There is no billing-integrity correction either (POL-RD-09(4)) — the fare breakdown carries no ERP gantries, no airport surcharge and no charge line without a counterpart in the trace or trip record. The driver's 90-day profile shows no repeat-deviation pattern (0 deviation flags over 471 completed trips on the fields POL-RD-06 names), so no POL-RD-06(b) uplift and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral arises; no other referral clause is triggered.

Outcome. The rider's claim is not supported by this trip's evidence on the correct baseline. Under POL-GEN-03, NO_ACTION means that because the rider filed, the fare stays as charged and no refund issues; the present state stands.

Both of you argued this as a route-deviation case. On the evidence, it is not one.

This was a RYDE_POOL booking. Under POL-RD-12 the baseline for the deviation test is the matched-itinerary optimal of 19.40 km that the platform computed for the pooled route at match time (EV-TRIP-00113), not the 15.80 km solo_optimal_distance_km the claim used as its comparator. The 15.80 km figure is carried on the record expressly 'for reference only'. A claim that measures excess against it has cited the wrong field, which is why the '28% longer' and '20.2 vs 15.8' framing cannot stand.

Under POL-RD-01 the distance actually driven is read from the GPS trace — 20.18 km (EV-GPS-00113), the governing figure — against the 19.40 km pooled baseline. The excess is 0.78 km, or 4.02%. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to exceed BOTH 20% of optimal AND 0.8 km absolute; it fails both limbs. No deviation is established, and no material deviation is anywhere near it.

The Hougang stop is why the trip looks longer, and it is fully accounted for. The platform itself sent MSG-00113-001 at 18:42:04 — before the vehicle moved — telling the rider a co-rider had been matched and the pooled route now included a Hougang Central pickup, estimated 19.4 km. POL-RD-12 excludes co-rider collection distance from the deviation test, and that distance is already inside the 19.40 km baseline the rider was given. The driver did not leave the corridor for a reason of his own; he drove the itinerary the platform sold. (POL-RD-04 is not in play either way: no chat message carries a waypoint_hint and no rider instruction names a road or place, so its corroboration test cannot be run in the driver's favour.)

Nothing else moves money. There is no traffic advisory covering the corridor (EV-ADVIS-00113-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT), so no closure exoneration is available and none is needed. The fare reconciles: erp_lines are empty, the airport surcharge is 0.00, and the 3.00 pool discount is already subtracted, so there is no phantom line to refund under POL-RD-09(4). The trip is METERED with quoted_fare_sgd null, so POL-RD-11 is not engaged, and the POL-RD-02 recomputation never runs because no deviation was established.

On the driver's profile, the only field POL-RD-06 uses reads deviation_flags_90d = 0 across 471 completed trips in 90 days, so no repeat-deviation pattern is established and no conduct referral arises. All other profile fields are context only under POL-GEN-01 and none was used to establish any fact about this trip.

The GPS trace is unimpaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07 (100% coverage, 217 fixes at the nominal 10-second interval, no gaps, max gap 0.0 s), and both artifacts that carry the deciding measurement — the trace and the trip record — are at weight 1.0, so no confidence discount applies.

Outcome: NO_ACTION. The rider filed; the charge of 26.83 stands, no refund issues, and the driver is owed no compensation. Confidence 0.90.

ruling.explanation:
Both of you agree on what happened; the argument is about which distance figure the policy measures against. This was a RYDE_POOL booking, so under POL-RD-12 the correct baseline is the matched-itinerary route the platform computed when it matched the co-rider — 19.40 km, on EV-TRIP-00113 and confirmed by the platform's own 18:42:04 message ('Estimated 19.4 km, 34 min'), which the rider read before the trip started. The 15.80 km figure in the rider's claim is the unmatched solo reference, carried on the trip record 'for reference only'; measuring against it is citing the wrong field, which is why the 28% figure does not stand.

POL-RD-01 reads the distance actually driven from the GPS trace, not the rounded trip-record copy. EV-GPS-00113 records 20.18 km against the 19.40 km baseline — an excess of 0.78 km, or 4.02%. POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only where the excess exceeds BOTH 20% of the baseline AND 0.8 km absolute. 4.02% fails the first and 0.78 km fails the second, so on this trip's own evidence no deviation is established, and POL-RD-01 directs NO_ACTION however the trip is characterised. The Hougang stop the rider objected to is the co-rider pickup on the matched pooled itinerary — the driver's 19:03:15 chat reply and the platform's pre-trip notice both say so — and POL-RD-12 excludes co-rider collection distance from any deviation measure. The rider is right that the driver wrote nothing exculpatory of his own choosing; that is simply because the stop was the itinerary the platform sold.

No separate correction is due. EV-FARE-00113's ERP lines are empty and no airport surcharge applies, so POL-RD-09(4) yields nothing. The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes (100% coverage, 217 fixes at the 10s interval, empty gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0), so no gap-handling or escalation under POL-RD-07 / POL-RD-10 is engaged. The POL-RD-02 recomputation the rider cites (recomputed fare 25.67 against 26.83 charged) is not reached, because POL-RD-02 only runs once a deviation is established; POL-RD-11 does not apply either, as EV-FARE-00113 shows METERED with quoted_fare_sgd null. POL-RD-06 is not reached (no material deviation, no balanced evidence) and the driver's clean trailing-90-day record is context only under POL-GEN-01. The driver billed 20.2 km against a 20.18 km trace, so there is no shortfall and no POL-RD-04 compensation. No closure was asserted and no advisory exists (EV-ADVIS-00113-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0), so POL-RD-03 does neither side any work. The charge stands: fare_breakdown.payment_status and refund_issued_sgd are left as they are. Confidence rests on the two weight-1.0 artifacts that carry the deciding measurement, EV-GPS-00113 and EV-TRIP-00113.

discards.claim: The rider's own chat entries corroborate the driver and defeat the claim's premise. At 19:02:40 the rider asks 'why are we at hougang'; the driver answers at 19:03:15 'pool booking, picking up the other passenger, app route'. That answer is consistent with the platform's 18:42:04 match notice, and it is the only party account of the Hougang stop anywhere on the record. The counterparty_statement is to the same effect. There is no artifact in the bundle that contradicts it, and no traffic advisory exists that could have forced the route (EV-ADVIS-00113-01 is MISSING; none covers the corridor). The driver's conduct was, on this record, exactly what POL-RD-12 describes and excuses.

ledger.claim: The three primary artifacts describe one and the same trip, not three different ones: EV-TRIP-00113, EV-GPS-00113 and EV-FARE-00113 each carry trip_id TRP-00113, and the trace's first fix at 18:47:10 matches the trip_record's started_at, so the rider's limb-(a) identification burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged on the face of the record.

Nothing in the trace needs discounting in the rider's favour or against it: coverage is 100%, there are 217 fixes at the nominal 10-second sampling interval, the gaps array is empty and max_gap_sec is 0.0, so none of POL-RD-07(a), (b) or (c) fires, the trace is unimpaired for policy purposes, and the driven distance can be read straight off the trace without any gap-handling concession.

Under POL-RD-01 the governing distance field is gps_trace.trace_distance_km, not the rounded trip_record convenience copy, and the trace records 20.18 km against the optimal route of 19.40 km stored on the trip_record: the measured excess is 0.78 km, or 4.02%.

POL-RD-12 excuses only distance attributable to collecting or setting down a co-rider, and in this case that distance is already inside the 19.40 km matched-itinerary baseline the rider was notified of at 18:42:04; the clause's own closing words are that it 'does not excuse excess beyond the matched itinerary', and the trace still runs 0.78 km beyond that matched baseline.

The diversion is the driver's own route and is corroborated independently of the rider's account: the driver wrote in the chat log at 19:03:15 'pool booking, picking up the other passenger, app route', and the rider's sole message in the log is the query 'why are we at hougang' at 19:02:40 — the rider contributed no route instruction at all.

No traffic advisory carries the diversion: EV-ADVIS-00113-01 is MISSING, holds weight 0.0, and its issue code is MISSING_ARTIFACT, with no LTA advisory covering the Punggol, Hougang or CTE corridors in the 18:41-19:23 window on 5 August 2026, so POL-RD-03's closure exoneration is unavailable to the driver.

The detour cannot be shifted onto the rider: the chat log contains no rider instruction to divert and no message carries a waypoint_hint, so POL-RD-04 cannot be run in the driver's favour, its corroboration test is undecidable on this record, and the driver holds no rider-instruction exoneration.

This is not an upfront-quoted trip, so the route-deviation money has not been closed off: fare_breakdown.fare_model is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, POL-RD-11 does not apply, and POL-RD-02 is the operative remedy clause, which would run against the 19.40 km matched-itinerary figure and not the 15.80 km solo reference figure.

If the excess is made out, the POL-RD-02 quantum is not de minimis on the platform's own numbers: the fare_breakdown's recomputed_fare on the matched 19.40 km and 34 min is SGD 25.67, the difference from the SGD 26.83 charged is 1.16, and the amount payable rounds up to SGD 1.20, which is above the SGD 0.50 floor.

Neither profile can decide this case in either direction: the driver's deviation_flags_90d is 0 across 471 completed_trips_90d, so no POL-RD-06 repeat-deviation pattern is established on the only fields that clause names, and under POL-GEN-01 the driver's otherwise clean record is credibility weighting only and may not be used to establish any fact about this trip or to carry an adverse finding against the rider.

I do not stretch the arithmetic: measured on the governing trace the excess is 0.78 km, which does not exceed POL-RD-01's 0.8 km absolute gate, and 4.02%, which does not exceed its 20% gate, so on this trip's own evidence the route deviation as pleaded is not established and the POL-RD-01 finding properly reads 'no deviation'.

This is a RYDE_POOL trip, so the only correct baseline for any deviation test is the matched-itinerary optimal that the platform computed and quoted at match time, 19.40 km on EV-TRIP-00113. The rider's arithmetic uses the 15.80 km solo_optimal_distance_km figure, which POL-RD-12 carries on the trip_record expressly 'for reference only' and which may not be used as the denominator of the POL-RD-01 test. A claim that measures excess against solo_optimal_distance_km has cited the wrong field and fails on that ground alone. Both figures are on the face of the record (optimal_distance_km 19.40; solo_optimal_distance_km 15.80), so the rider can see exactly why the 28% figure in the claim text is an artefact of the wrong comparator.

Measured the way POL-RD-01 requires, against the trace figure that governs and not the rounded convenience copy on the trip_record, the excess is 0.78 km. gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 20.18 km (EV-GPS-00113) and the matched-itinerary optimal is 19.40 km (EV-TRIP-00113), giving an excess of 0.78 km, or 4.02% of optimal. POL-RD-01 requires BOTH that the excess exceed 20% of optimal AND that it exceed 0.8 km absolute. This excess fails on both limbs: 4.02% is far below 20%, and 0.78 km is below the 0.8 km floor. No deviation is established, and no MATERIAL deviation is anywhere near established. POL-RD-01 then directs the outcome: NO_ACTION, however the rider characterises the trip.

Even on the rider's own theory that the Hougang leg is the objectionable part, POL-RD-12 excludes it before the threshold is applied: distance attributable to collecting a co-rider on a platform-matched pooled itinerary 'is never a deviation'. The record confirms the Hougang stop was precisely that — the driver's track is an unbroken 10-second telemetry trace (point_count 217, coverage_pct 100, gaps empty, max_gap_sec 0) whose only dwell is the co-rider boarding stop, and the driver's first and last fixes run 18:47:10 to 19:23:10 with no excursus off the matched corridor. The driver is not exonerated for going somewhere he chose; the stop he made was the itinerary the platform sold.

The route was disclosed to the rider in advance, in writing, by the platform itself. Chat message MSG-00113-001, sent 2026-08-05T18:42:04, states: 'Co-rider matched. Your pooled route now includes one pickup at Hougang Central before your drop-off. Estimated 19.4 km, 34 min.' It was read by the rider 27 seconds later, at 18:42:31, and the trip only started at 18:47:10. The claim that the driver 'went off to Hougang in the middle of my trip for no reason' is contradicted by the platform's own pre-trip notice; the Hougang pickup was announced before the vehicle moved. This is not a rider-instruction exoneration under POL-RD-04 — no waypoint_hint is present — but it is the factual answer to the only allegation of arbitrary conduct in the claim.

The rider's own chat entries corroborate the driver and defeat the claim's premise. At 19:02:40 the rider asks 'why are we at hougang'; the driver answers at 19:03:15 'pool booking, picking up the other passenger, app route'. That answer is consistent with the platform's 18:42:04 match notice, and it is the only party account of the Hougang stop anywhere on the record. The counterparty_statement is to the same effect. There is no artifact in the bundle that contradicts it, and no traffic advisory exists that could have forced the route (EV-ADVIS-00113-01 is MISSING; none covers the corridor). The driver's conduct was, on this record, exactly what POL-RD-12 describes and excuses.

ledger.claim: The trace itself is unimpaired under POL-RD-07: coverage is 100%, the expected and actual sampling intervals both equal 10 seconds, there are no gaps recorded, and the maximum gap is 0.0 seconds. None of limbs (a), (b) or (c) fires, so the excess is measured from a clean trace and needs no independent corroboration. The GPS_TRACE artifact is also COMPLETE at weight 1.0, so there is no POL-GEN-02 discount to disclose or apply. The rider cannot argue the measurement is unsafe: it is the best-quality evidence in the bundle, and it is the artifact that defeats the claim.

The POL-RD-06 driver_profile check is not even reached, and where reached it is clean. The clause is consulted only where POL-RD-01 records a MATERIAL deviation or the evidence is otherwise finely balanced; here there is no deviation at all, let alone a material one, and the evidence is not balanced — one trace, one tolerance, both limbs failed. For completeness, the driver's trailing-90-day figure is deviation_flags_90d = 0 against completed_trips_90d = 471, so no pattern can be established on the fields the clause names, and POL-GEN-01 forbids substituting any other profile field for the test. No POL-RD-06(a) uplift, no POL-RD-06(b) FULL_REFUND uplift and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral is available to the rider on this record.

There is no alternative monetary route left to the rider. POL-RD-02 is the only clause that converts an established deviation into a refund, and no deviation is established, so the recomputation never runs. The fare-breakdown arithmetic confirms there is nothing else to correct: erp_lines carries no entries at all (total 0.00), the airport surcharge is 0.00 on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport, the promo_discount of 3.00 has already been subtracted from the charge, and the residual money comparison on EV-FARE-00113 yields a refund before rounding of only 1.16 against a charged_total of 26.83 — which is unreachable in any event because the threshold gate in POL-RD-01 fails. POL-GEN-03 then fixes the meaning of the outcome: the rider filed, the charge stands, the present state is preserved, and the ruling value is NO_ACTION.
